channel.title: Wire — tech digest
channel.description: One digest a day, merged from thirty sources.

item.title: Engineering Production Systems for an Agentic Era: QCon San Francisco 2026
item.description: QCon San Francisco 2026 will bring together practitioners from Airbnb, OpenAI, Netflix, Honeycomb, and other engineering organizations to share how they are building, operating, and evolving production systems as AI agents take on a larger… (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Packaging AI Agent Permissions as OCI Images
item.description: Docker has announced that it is bringing the Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF, aiming to make what an AI agent may access as portable as the agent itself. By Claudio Masolo (1 source: infoq)

item.title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
item.description: DigitalOcean recently launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview, offering a managed cloud infrastructure layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access, and serverless AI inference. By Sergio De Simone (1 source: infoq)

item.title: DeepSeek Harness
item.description: Use DeepSeek Harness to work with documents, analyze spreadsheets, write code, and schedule tasks. Extend its capabilities with composable plugins. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Recap for Developers
item.description: OpenAI announced a series of product and developer updates at DevDay 2026, including GPT-6.1 Sol, computer use for the Agents API, cloud-based Codex environments, a Decisions API, and new plugin capabilities for ChatGPT. By Daniel Dominguez (1 source: infoq)

item.title: AWS Well-Architected Agent is now available in preview
item.description: AWS announces the preview of AWS Well-Architected Agent, a AI-powered service that is the next-gen evolution of AWS Trusted Advisor and the AWS Well-Architected Tool. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon Redshift now supports cross-Region queries for your data lake
item.description: Amazon Redshift now supports querying Amazon S3 data lake tables located in a different AWS Region. With enhanced VPC routing, data lake query traffic between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift stays within your own VPC. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon DynamoDB introduces filtered export to Amazon S3
item.description: Amazon DynamoDB now supports filtered export for tables. Export to Amazon S3 allows you to export your table data for analytics, data sharing, and other offline uses, as either a full export or an incremental export over a time window. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
item.description: Today, AWS announces the availability of Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in 17 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Asia… (1 source: aws)

item.title: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now included in the AWS Security Hub Threat Analytics plan
item.description: Today, AWS announces that Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now included in the AWS Security Hub Threat Analytics plan. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon GuardDuty now supports centralized management using AWS Organizations declarative policies
item.description: Amazon GuardDuty now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies, enabling you to centrally enable GuardDuty threat detection across every account and Region in your AWS organization. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Fixing One Function's Disk Spills with ALTER FUNCTION … SET work_mem
item.description: Use PostgreSQL ALTER FUNCTION SET work_mem to stop one function's sorts spilling to disk without a global change. A production fix: 150 GB a day to 0. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: When to Choose x86 or ARM for Postgres
item.description: ARM and x86 can give you different performance at the same vCPU count. Here's what differs, what to measure, and how to choose. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Kafgres 0.2: 700 MB/s of Kafka Throughput on Postgres
item.description: Profiling and optimizing the Kafgres Postgres extension to achieve 700 MB/s write throughput and 600k evt/s on a single machine. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: pgBackRest and Failover: Why archive_mode Matters
item.description: A recent question on the community channels described a difficult situation: a standby had been promoted with archive_mode=off, and restarting the new primary was something the team wanted to avoid. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Safe Not Safe: Is My Migration Safe?
item.description: A local-first Postgres migration safety checker for developers. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Pgpool-II 4.7.3, 4.6.8, 4.5.13, 4.4.18, 4.3.21
item.description: Pgpool-II 4.7.3, 4.6.8, 4.5.13, 4.4.18 and 4.3.21 officially released. (1 source: postgresweekly)

item.title: Support for modern cryptographic algorithms in Workers
item.description: Cloudflare Workers is adding opt-in support for post-quantum-resistant algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA. You can try it today. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Introducing Cloudflare Basin: an open, serverless data platform, now generally available
item.description: Cloudflare Basin is built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. With general availability, developers can ingest, manage, and query large datasets at scale without paying data egress fees. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes
item.description: Cloudflare Containers now start 6x faster, let your agent choose each sandbox's image and instance type at runtime, and support filesystem snapshots in public beta, all controlled from a Durable Object. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: AI Search is now generally available
item.description: AI Search is now generally available. It embeds image pixels directly for visual search, runs optical character recognition on scanned PDFs, accepts files up to 10 MiB, and works with any chat model. Here's what's new and how pricing works. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Identify AI model overuse with User Insights
item.description: AI Gateway User Insights now adds task, model, turn, and user categories to help teams understand AI adoption and make better model decisions. This is available free to AI Gateway users. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: The Internet has a second audience
item.description: More than half the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated, and AI agents are the fastest-growing part of it. We're giving site owners the tools to see who's visiting, decide who gets in, and charge for access. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.description: It's an interesting and potentially useful trick to have an element know where it is on a grid. That's tricky enough when the items are in one row/column, but what about when they span? (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Connection Allowlists: Lock Down Where a Page Can Connect
item.description: Chrome 152 introduces connection allowlists, a new security mechanism that lets you create a strict network sandbox for your documents and workers. (1 source: frontendfocus)
